lines: וְהוֹי לְךָ, כַּמָּה סוֹלֵחַ וְגוֹאֵל אָתָּה

review: The hymn is Isaiah 53 set as an address to the Crucified: 1:1–11 is Isa 53:5 with Ps 22:17 and Matt 27:38–44 (the taunt of the passers-by), 2:1–11 is Isa 53:3–4 with Luke 23:34, and 3:1–11 is Isa 53:9 with Ps 22:17 and Ps 116:12.

Each stanza ends with the same line repeated three times, as the print repeats the taunt (لِتَنْجُ إِذَا كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الْإِلٰه) and then the answering line (تَجَرَّعْتَ كَأْسِي / لَكَ الْقَلْبُ); the payload keeps the triples verbatim, since the repetition is the stanza's rhetorical close.

3:7 נִדְקְרוּ יָדֶיךָ כֹּפֶר לְיָדַי — the Arabic تُدَقُّ يَدَاكَ فِدَاءَ يَدِي is 'Your hands are struck for my hands' ransom'; the Hebrew uses דָּקַר (Zech 12:10, Ps 22:17) and the glossary's כֹּפֶר, so the line is the piercing and the price at once.
1:3 keeps the second person address inside the vision (אֶרְאֶךָ … נִצְלַבְתָּ), because the Arabic أَرَاكَ is a seeing and the stanza must not slide into narration.
